title: BCG Year-End Sales Events Consumer Study 2026: For Year-End Sales Events, Trust Is the New Currency
gist: BCG's sixth annual survey of 10,220 consumers shows year-end sales events have plateaued at near-saturated awareness, trust in advertised prices is only 54%, and GenAI (56% expected use) is replacing social media as the shopper's verification tool, so proof beats persuasion.

insights.claim: Black Friday awareness is 95% and shopping intent among those aware rose only two points to 81%, half of last year's four-point rise, so growth from the event calendar is plateauing.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: Retail event-driven volume growth is limited; competition shifts to share.
insights.locator: Relevance of Year-End Sales Events Is Plateauing

insights.claim: 62% of shoppers begin deal searches in October or early November, only about a third wait until days before or the event day, and 76% of planners hold back purchases at least sometimes, pulling spend toward a season rather than a day.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: Front-load promotions into October; watch margin dilution from longer promotional periods.
insights.locator: Relevance of Year-End Sales Events Is Plateauing

insights.claim: Gifting is the main reason to shop (63%), with essentials taking the largest budget share and clothing, electronics and beauty the top three categories; plans barely changed from 2025.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: Stable category mix implies no demand surprise.
insights.locator: Relevance of Year-End Sales Events Is Plateauing

insights.claim: Only 54% of consumers trust advertised prices at year-end events; trust is about two-thirds in the US but only about a third in Denmark, the Czech Republic and Germany.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: European promotions face more skepticism than US ones.

insights.claim: Net trust drivers: retailer reputation and money-back/free-returns each 65%, verified reviews 59%, clear regular-vs-discount price comparison 58%; whereas real-time scarcity messages score 8%, AI review summaries 4% and influencer recommendations 3%.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: Credibility signals outperform persuasion tactics; reallocate marketing spend.

insights.claim: 22% of shoppers planning to spend less believe deals are available all the time, and the minimum discount expected from a good deal eased two points to about 30%, so belief in the markdown matters more than its size.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: Deeper discounts are commoditized; credibility isn't.

themes.theme: GenAI replaces social as shopping tool

insights.claim: 56% of consumers expect to use GenAI for year-end shopping (up eight points), led by Gen Z at 66% and millennials at 62%; 86% find it useful, 83% say it helps find better deals and 78% say it raises purchase completion.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: AI assistants are becoming a gatekeeper for retail discovery and conversion.

insights.claim: Social media as shopping inspiration fell nine points to 46% and declined in every market while GenAI as inspiration rose four points to 11% in every market.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: Ad budgets will migrate from social/influencer to AI-mediated discovery.

insights.claim: Consumers trust GenAI most for comparing prices across retailers (39%) and product features (37%), and trust assistant recommendations that allow independent verification (33%) and visible price history (31%) more than the assistant's track record (21%); transactional tasks like checkout are still developing.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: Agentic checkout is not yet trusted; comparison is the use case.

insights.claim: Retailers should structure product, price and promotion data for AI to surface, audit how AI compares their brand, and agree platform terms before pay-to-play becomes the norm, while requesting a verified review after every purchase.
insights.speaker: BCG
insights.so_what: Emerging 'AI-engine optimization' spend and platform fees for retail.
